name: Ironfang Render API
description:
Ironfang Render renders web pages to images, PDFs and video. Give it a URL or a
block of HTML and get the finished asset without running a browser.

## No attribution on your output

Nothing you render through the API carries an Ironfang badge or watermark,
whatever your billing state. Only the anonymous free tools on
ironfang.com mark their output.

## Authentication

Every request carries an API key as a bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer rw_live_...
```

Keys are created in the portal at https://portal.ironfang.com. They are shown
once at creation and stored only as a hash, so a lost key is replaced rather
than recovered.

## Responses are bytes, not JSON

`/v1/screenshot`, `/v1/pdf`, `/v1/image/{id}` and `/v1/video` return the
rendered file directly. `/v1/site-preview` returns a multipart payload with
the poster and MP4. Only errors and the metadata endpoints return JSON.

## Billing

Ironfang Render has no plans or credits. Usage is billed to your
organisation's Ironfang billing account, which every product shares
(`/billing/v1`, managed in the portal). Each kind of work counts against a
meter, and each meter has a monthly free allowance (UTC calendar months);
beyond it, usage is pay-as-you-go at graduated rates once paid usage is
enabled on the billing account. The catalogue of meters, allowances and
rates is `GET /billing/v1/catalogue`.

| Work | Meter | Counts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Screenshot, signed screenshot | `render.screenshot` | 1 per screenshot |
| PDF | `render.pdf` | 1 per PDF of at most 100 pages |
| Template image, signed image | `render.image` | 1 per image |
| QR code | `render.qr` | 1 per code; a free utility, never charged |
| Clip, 1080p (`vertical`, `landscape`) | `render.video_second_fhd` | output seconds, rounded up per clip |
| Clip, `720p` or `square` | `render.video_second_hd` | output seconds, rounded up per clip |
| Site preview | `render.site_preview_second` | output seconds, rounded up per preview |

Every billable request is admitted before any work starts: the most it
can count is reserved, and a request that cannot be admitted is refused
with nothing done. What the work actually produced is committed when it
succeeds - never more than was reserved - and a failure, a refused input
or a cancellation commits nothing. A clip reserves its duration; a site
preview reserves the 60 second limit and commits its real length. Billable
responses say what they counted in `X-Ironfang-Meter` and
`X-Ironfang-Quantity`; `GET /v1/usage` reports the period.

A billing refusal answers with a stable code in the usual error body:
`free_allowance_exhausted`, `account_budget_exhausted` or
`product_budget_exhausted` (429); `paid_usage_paused`, `payment_required`,
`payment_action_required` or `account_restricted` (402);
`product_not_eligible` (403); `account_closed` (410);
`operation_too_large` (413); `billing_temporarily_unavailable` (503, with
`Retry-After`). An API key on an account that belongs to no Ironfang
organisation is `403 account_not_linked`.

A PDF may have at most 100 pages. A longer document is refused with
`422 pdf_too_long` and nothing is counted.

## Caching

An identical request made again within **ten minutes** of the render that
produced it may be served from cache: `X-Ironfang-Cache: hit`,
`X-Ironfang-Quantity: 0`, nothing reserved and nothing counted. The cache
is per instance and bounded in size, so an entry can be evicted sooner and
a hit is never guaranteed; after ten minutes the same request is a new,
billable render. PDFs are never cached. Set `no_cache: true` to force a
fresh render, which is billable; the flag is deliberately excluded from
the cache key, so two fresh requests do not hit each other's results.

## Rate limits

Two rate limits apply, both per minute:

- **120 renders per account**, and
- **60 renders per target host**, counted across all customers.

The second protects the sites being rendered: one API call is a full page
load, so a victim's exposure must not scale with our customer count. Both
are checked after the cache and before admission, so a blocked call
reserves and costs nothing.

## Capacity limits

Three more limits are the same for every account, and no billing setting
lifts them. They are refused with Ironfang Render's own codes, never a
billing code, and a refused call reserves and costs nothing.

- **2 browser operations in progress per account.** Screenshots, PDFs,
  template images and site previews count together, however they
  arrived: synchronous requests (signed URLs included) and durable jobs a
  worker is running, across the whole service. A synchronous request
  over the limit is `429 concurrency_limit` with `Retry-After`; a signed
  URL, whose caller is a browser or a link-preview crawler, first waits
  up to 10 seconds for one to finish. A durable job over it is not
  refused: it waits in the queue until one of the account's operations
  finishes. QR codes and clips use no browser and do
  not count. A cache hit uses no browser either.
- **1,000 unfinished jobs per account** (queued, running or being
  cancelled). A job or a batch that would take the account past it is
  `429 queue_full`, with `Retry-After`; a batch is refused whole, and no
  job of it is created.

## Bot protection

Ironfang Render does not attempt to circumvent bot protection, CAPTCHAs or
paywalls. A challenge page renders as the challenge page. This is a
deliberate limit, not a bug.

## For agents and tools

The canonical base URL is https://api.ironfang.com/render. Every operation
has a stable `operationId`. Every error an operation returns is JSON of the
shape `{"error": {"code", "message", "docs"}, "request_id"}`: branch on
`code` and the HTTP status, never on `message`. The machine-readable index
of the Ironfang APIs is https://ironfang.com/.well-known/api-catalog, and
https://ironfang.com/llms.txt is a plain-text map of them for a language
model. Ironfang Render is also available as MCP tools at
https://mcp.ironfang.com/mcp (see https://ironfang.com/docs/mcp). Renderwolf
is the name the product launched under, not a separate product; its
`/renderwolf` prefix and `X-Renderwolf-*` headers were retired on
28 September 2026, and the prefix now answers `410`.
